questions.q: What does the editorial give as the purpose of the magazine as it enters a new year?
options: To raise funds for relief work
Not quite. The article says: To turn minds in a positive direction and help people understand the Creator’s plan.
To report the news of the Muslim world
Not quite. The article says: To turn minds in a positive direction and help people understand the Creator’s plan.
To defend one community against another
Not quite. The article says: To turn minds in a positive direction and help people understand the Creator’s plan.
To turn minds in a positive direction and help people understand the Creator’s plan
Yes. It also presents the Quran’s message of peace.
questions.rationale: “The purpose of this magazine is to re-engineer people’s minds along positive lines and make them understand the creation plan of the Creator.”

questions.q: Hans Bethe was overjoyed to learn why the stars shine. What contrast does the article draw with believers?
options: Discovery matters less than obedience
Not quite. The article says: A small discovery thrilled the scientist, yet many who say they have found God show no such joy.
Scientists are happier people than believers
Not quite. The article says: A small discovery thrilled the scientist, yet many who say they have found God show no such joy.
A small discovery thrilled the scientist, yet many who say they have found God show no such joy
Right. Without that joy, the discovery has not really been made.
Believers should avoid looking at the stars
Not quite. The article says: A small discovery thrilled the scientist, yet many who say they have found God show no such joy.
questions.rationale: “If there are no traces of the joy of discovery, then the discovery itself has yet to be made.”

questions.q: How does the article describe man’s position with regard to the natural world?
options: He is separate from it, and unaffected
Not quite. The article says: He is a beneficiary, free to use it but not to upset its balance – he cannot create even a leaf.
He is its servant, with no right to use it
Not quite. The article says: He is a beneficiary, free to use it but not to upset its balance – he cannot create even a leaf.
He is a beneficiary, free to use it but not to upset its balance – he cannot create even a leaf
Yes. Polluting it is called suicidal.
He is its owner, free to do as he likes
Not quite. The article says: He is a beneficiary, free to use it but not to upset its balance – he cannot create even a leaf.
questions.rationale: “Man is permitted to exploit natural resources but without destroying the natural order of things… Man’s freedom ends where his mismanagement of nature begins.”

questions.q: The article says reason can have a good or a bad outcome. On what does this depend?
options: On how much schooling one has had
Not quite. The article says: Used with sincerity and modesty it builds a person; joined to ego it makes him arrogant.
Used with sincerity and modesty it builds a person; joined to ego it makes him arrogant
Well read. It must also be developed by study and reflection.
On the subject one reasons about
Not quite. The article says: Used with sincerity and modesty it builds a person; joined to ego it makes him arrogant.
On whether one reasons alone or with others
Not quite. The article says: Used with sincerity and modesty it builds a person; joined to ego it makes him arrogant.
questions.rationale: “When used with sincerity and modesty, it serves as a constructive and healthy agent of one’s personality. But if one is a victim of egoism, then reason makes him an arrogant person.”

questions.q: A creeper that had been cut down and cemented over broke through the floor and grew again. What does the article see in this?
options: The danger of plants near houses
Not quite. The article says: The force of life, which persists and reappears just when it seems to have ended.
The force of life, which persists and reappears just when it seems to have ended
Correct. It “will claim its right to exist.”
The poor quality of the cement
Not quite. The article says: The force of life, which persists and reappears just when it seems to have ended.
The carelessness of the owner
Not quite. The article says: The force of life, which persists and reappears just when it seems to have ended.
questions.rationale: “Even when uprooted, it continues to exist, albeit dormant… When people conclude that… life must have ended, that is just when it rears its head from the debris.”

questions.q: A good driver who sees a ball roll into the road stops at once. Why, and what is the wider lesson?
options: The ball might damage the car – avoid small losses
Not quite. The article says: He foresees the child behind the ball – in life, too, one must read what a sign implies.
Others are watching – guard your reputation
Not quite. The article says: He foresees the child behind the ball – in life, too, one must read what a sign implies.
The law requires it – obey every rule
Not quite. The article says: He foresees the child behind the ball – in life, too, one must read what a sign implies.
He foresees the child behind the ball – in life, too, one must read what a sign implies
Yes. And keep to one’s own “lane.”
questions.rationale: “The really good driver stops, not on account of the ball, but on account of the child that he sees with his mind’s eye.”

questions.q: What does the article name as the price of peace?
options: Paying compensation
Not quite. The article says: Tolerating loss.
Winning the argument first
Not quite. The article says: Tolerating loss.
Tolerating loss
Right. It takes courage, and leaves one free to rebuild.
Avoiding other people
Not quite. The article says: Tolerating loss.
questions.rationale: “What is the price of peace? Tolerating loss!… To patiently accept and tolerate loss is not defeatism.”

questions.q: What test does the article suggest before one speaks?
options: Whether it can be said quickly
Not quite. The article says: Whether what one is about to say rests on evidence and will do good; if not, stay silent.
Whether what one is about to say rests on evidence and will do good; if not, stay silent
Yes. An allegation is not the same as a supported statement.
Whether others have already said it
Not quite. The article says: Whether what one is about to say rests on evidence and will do good; if not, stay silent.
Whether it will impress the listeners
Not quite. The article says: Whether what one is about to say rests on evidence and will do good; if not, stay silent.
questions.rationale: “Begin by examining whether what you have to say is supported by logic. If you have good reason to speak, then open your mouth, else remain silent.”

questions.q: When Joseph was thrown into the well, what does the Quran say was revealed to him?
options: That he would come out to a new life and rise so high his brothers would not know him
Exactly. His worst moment was about to become his best.
That he would return home the next day
Not quite. The article says: That he would come out to a new life and rise so high his brothers would not know him.
That he should stay silent about his dream
Not quite. The article says: That he would come out to a new life and rise so high his brothers would not know him.
That his brothers would soon be punished
Not quite. The article says: That he would come out to a new life and rise so high his brothers would not know him.
questions.rationale: “God revealed to Joseph that his worst moments were about to become his best. Where antagonists intended to end his life, a whole fresh chapter unfolded.”

questions.q: Why does the article call the age of civilisation “still incomplete”?
options: Man has learnt to turn matter into technology, but not yet to settle differences by peaceful reasoning
Well reasoned. War is as outdated as striking stones to make fire.
Machines often break down
Not quite. The article says: Man has learnt to turn matter into technology, but not yet to settle differences by peaceful reasoning.
Not everyone can read
Not quite. The article says: Man has learnt to turn matter into technology, but not yet to settle differences by peaceful reasoning.
Many countries are still poor
Not quite. The article says: Man has learnt to turn matter into technology, but not yet to settle differences by peaceful reasoning.
questions.rationale: “Though man learnt to convert matter into technology, he failed to discover the art of managing differences.”
